answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network applies topological cut verifications across peer interactions. Every peer evaluates transaction flow across a graph ridge, where genuine coordination forms an authentic signal of work. Auditing agents cross-verify dense clusters, slashing the bonded stake of colluding identities. Because auditing audits require exponential attacker cost across graph bottlenecks, Sybil swarms collapse as fast as a burning comet.
